name: Route 66 West — January
subtitle: Tulsa · Cadillac Ranch · Albuquerque · Petrified Forest · Canyon de Chelly · Monument Valley · Grand Canyon · Oatman · Death Valley · Las Vegas · Santa Monica
summary: Fifteen days one way, from Dallas to the end of Route 66 on Santa Monica Pier. North to Tulsa to find the old road, then west across Oklahoma, the Texas Panhandle and New Mexico on it — Cadillac Ranch, Central Avenue through Albuquerque, and the only national park Route 66 runs through. It leaves the road for Canyon de Chelly, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon, seen from two nights in Williams, rejoins it for the longest empty stretch left, through Seligman, Oatman and Amboy, and swings north to Death Valley and a night in Las Vegas before the last run into Los Angeles. 2,647 miles, and cold for the first eight nights — the overnight stops are picked to miss the coldest towns on the way.

mustSee.name: Blue Whale of Catoosa
mustSee.why: A concrete whale on a pond beside Route 66, built as an anniversary present. Walk into its mouth; it costs nothing.

mustSee.name: Cadillac Ranch
mustSee.why: Ten Cadillacs buried nose-down in a Panhandle field. Bring a can of spray paint and add a layer at sunset.

mustSee.name: The Painted Desert
mustSee.why: Red and lavender badlands from a string of overlooks, and the only stretch of Route 66 inside a national park.

mustSee.name: Wigwam Motel
mustSee.why: A night in a concrete teepee with 1950s cars parked outside. Two of them sleep six.

mustSee.name: Spider Rock
mustSee.why: An 800-foot sandstone spire in Canyon de Chelly, at the end of a free rim drive most people never hear of.

mustSee.name: Monument Valley
mustSee.why: Sunset over the Mittens on arrival, and the Valley Drive when the gate opens the next morning.

mustSee.name: The Grand Canyon Railway
mustSee.why: A train from the middle of Williams to the South Rim and back — about two and a quarter hours each way through ponderosa pine, while the motorhome stays plugged in at the depot.

mustSee.name: Hopi Point
mustSee.why: Sunset from the widest view on the South Rim, reached by car only from December to February.

mustSee.name: The burros of Oatman
mustSee.why: Wild burros wander the main street of an old gold town and put their heads in the car window.

mustSee.name: Badwater Basin
mustSee.why: The lowest point in North America, 282 feet below sea level, and warm in January. Walk out onto the salt.

mustSee.name: The Fountains of Bellagio
mustSee.why: Water thrown high above the lake in time to music, every fifteen minutes after dark — free, outdoors, and fine for children, which most of the Strip is not.

mustSee.name: End of the Trail
mustSee.why: The sign on Santa Monica Pier that every Route 66 trip ends at, 2,647 miles after Dallas.

watchOuts.title: Book these first
watchOuts.text: Williams first, because nights 7 and 8 fall on Martin Luther King weekend: the Grand Canyon Railway for Saturday the 16th, and either a room in town or the RV park beside the station. Then Monument Valley for night 6, at The View or Goulding's, then the Wigwam Motel for night 5, which has fifteen wigwams in all. In the motorhome, add Dockweiler RV Park for night 14: it takes bookings no more than 90 days ahead, which for 22 January means late October. Everything else on this route has slack in January.

watchOuts.title: Eight freezing nights, then none
watchOuts.text: On the January averages every night from Tulsa (−2°C) to Williams (−6°C) goes below freezing — eight in a row, with Oklahoma City, Amarillo, Albuquerque, Holbrook and Monument Valley in between, the coldest about −7°C at Holbrook and Monument Valley. Kingman on night 9 is a coin toss at about −1°C. After that it is Barstow at 2°C, Death Valley and Las Vegas at 4°C and Santa Monica at 9°C. The overnight stops are chosen to miss the coldest towns on the way: Gallup averages −10°C and Santa Fe about −8°C, and neither is slept in. Williams is barely a degree warmer than the Grand Canyon rim, so the gain there is hookups and the train, not the temperature. Pack for a winter trip that turns into a mild one, not the other way round.

watchOuts.title: Freeze damage is charged to you
watchOuts.text: Hire companies treat a split pipe as your damage, and El Monte's own conditions list damage caused by freezing among the things its cover never pays for, whichever cover you buy. A rig hired near Dallas will not be winterized — which you need, because you are living in it — and it drives straight into eight nights below freezing. Run the propane furnace all night at 13 to 15°C, never off and never the heat pump, which gives up around 4°C. Disconnect the city-water hose at night and run off a fresh tank kept at least half full, and leave the cabinet doors under the sinks open. One propane tank feeds the furnace, the water heater and the stove — 14 gallons on El Monte's Class C Large — so fill it at Albuquerque and again at Williams rather than finding it empty at three in the morning. If the water heater is the tankless kind El Monte lists on that model, ask at handover whether it has freeze protection; that usually needs 12-volt power, which the hookups give it. Get it in writing that the water system is live and that the company knows where you are taking it.

watchOuts.title: If a line freezes
watchOuts.text: A tap that gives nothing, or a pump that runs on without building pressure, means something has frozen — on the dead tap's line if the others still work. Switch the water pump off first: running it against ice does nothing and can break it. Open the dead taps, hot and cold, so the melt has somewhere to go. Then warm it gently: the furnace up, the cabinet doors open, and a hair dryer on low kept moving, working back from the tap towards the pump. Never a heat gun, a flame or boiling water, which crack the plastic fittings, and never force a frozen dump-valve handle. A line inside the coach clears in under an hour that way; anything outside or underneath usually thaws by itself by midday, when January afternoons along here reach 6 to 11°C in strong sun. Most RV plumbing is plastic PEX, which usually survives a freeze — it is the fittings, the pump and the valves that crack. Turn the pump back on with every tap shut: if it keeps kicking on by itself, something is leaking, and it is bottled water, the campground's bathrooms and a call to El Monte's roadside line.

watchOuts.title: The depots set the ends of the trip
watchOuts.text: El Monte's Dallas depot is in McKinney, 30 miles up US-75 — on day 1's road — and is open Monday to Saturday, 9 to 4, and shut on Sundays. Standard pickup is after 1pm, earlier for a fee, and the handover takes one to two hours. Returns are in the morning — 9 to 10:30 at McKinney — and the Los Angeles yard is in Santa Fe Springs, 23 miles from LAX. So day 1 leaves at about 3, and day 15 needs a flight after about 1pm.

watchOuts.title: Every toll is on day 1, and all of it is avoidable
watchOuts.text: Leaving Dallas, the Dallas North Tollway, the Bush Turnpike and the Sam Rayburn Tollway are all cashless, and so is Oklahoma's Indian Nation Turnpike. The hire company pays them and bills you with a daily fee on top, which can turn a few dollars of toll into $20 to $40. US-75 from Dallas to Tulsa is free and takes about half an hour longer, and the map shows it. Day 2 runs the old road beside the Turner Turnpike rather than on it, and from Oklahoma City to the Pacific there is no toll road on the route.

watchOuts.title: A few things are shut on the day you pass them
watchOuts.text: The Oklahoma Route 66 Museum in Clinton closes on Sundays and Mondays from November to January, and for the first week of January — day 3 is a Monday, so this route uses the National Route 66 Museum at Elk City instead, which is open. Delgadillo's Snow Cap in Seligman closes for the winter. Two more only just work: the Chandler Interpretive Center opens from 1 to 5 on Sundays, and the U-Drop Inn is shut on Sundays but you pass it on a Monday. The Bellagio's conservatory shuts while it changes displays, and January is when it changes. Move the dates and all of this moves with them.

watchOuts.title: Monument Valley is an evening and a morning
watchOuts.text: You arrive at about four on day 6, after the Valley Drive's last entry at 2:30, so the first evening is sunset from the rim. Drive the loop when the gate opens at 8 the next morning and you are out by 11, with time for Desert View and the rim road before dark. The parts beyond the self-drive loop — Mystery Valley, Hunts Mesa, the arches — are open only with a Navajo guide, about $79 an adult and $59 a child for two and a half hours.

watchOuts.title: The Monument Valley loop is dirt
watchOuts.text: Most hire agreements exclude unpaved roads, so the 17-mile Valley Drive — which families drive in hire cars every day — is at your own risk if something breaks. Go slowly, stay on the loop, and don't try it after rain or snow; the guided tour is the fallback.

watchOuts.title: Day 14 is a long drive on the second-last day
watchOuts.text: 290 miles and about six hours from Las Vegas to Santa Monica, arriving on a Friday. Leave by eight and aim to be through Pasadena before two, when the weekend traffic starts. If you are running late, nothing on this day has a closing time except the traffic — the pier is open into the evening on Fridays. The Wigwam Motel in Rialto would split the day in two, if the flight home allows it.

watchOuts.title: Snow closes the high roads
watchOuts.text: This route crosses the Continental Divide on I-40 east of Gallup at about 7,250 feet on day 5, drives AZ-64 past Desert View at 7,400 on day 7 and sleeps two nights at 6,800 in Williams. A January storm can shut any of them for hours, and US-191 and US-160 across the Navajo Nation are ploughed slowly. Check nmroads.com and az511.gov the night before each of days 4 to 9. Day 9 is only 131 miles: if the weather costs you half a day, that is where it goes.

watchOuts.title: Death Valley is still repairing roads
watchOuts.text: As of 2026, Lower Wildrose Road, Darwin Falls Road and Titus Canyon were closed after floods, and South Badwater Road had reopened with missing pavement and soft shoulders. None of those is on this route, but the list changes after every storm: check the park's conditions page the week before. Day 11 comes in over Panamint Valley Road and Towne Pass, which were open.

watchOuts.title: The park pass covers three parks, not the Navajo ones
watchOuts.text: Petrified Forest ($25), the Grand Canyon ($35) and Death Valley ($30) come to $90 at the gates, against $80 for the annual America the Beautiful pass. Monument Valley and the Little Colorado River Gorge are Navajo tribal parks at $8 to $10 a head and do not take it. Canyon de Chelly and Hubbell Trading Post are free. The Grand Canyon Railway builds a $15 park fee into each adult fare whether or not you hold the pass.

watchOuts.title: Two time zones, both in your favour
watchOuts.text: You gain an hour at the New Mexico line on day 4 and another crossing the Colorado River into California on day 10. Every summer the Navajo Nation keeps daylight saving and the rest of Arizona does not, and visitors miss their tour times by an hour. In January nobody is on daylight saving and the clocks agree.

watchOuts.title: California fuel costs more
watchOuts.text: California fuel costs more than a dollar a gallon above Arizona's, and well above Nevada's. Fill up in Kingman before day 10 and again in Barstow before Death Valley, where the pumps at Furnace Creek and Stovepipe Wells are the dearest on the trip, and again in Las Vegas before the run into Los Angeles on day 14. Roy's at Amboy sells fuel, but at Amboy prices. On the Navajo Nation, fill up in Chinle or Kayenta rather than hoping for something in between.

pros: Route 66 for real: roughly 1,400 of its 2,448 miles, from Tulsa to the End of the Trail sign on Santa Monica Pier.
All three must-stops — Monument Valley, the Grand Canyon and Death Valley — plus the only national park Route 66 runs through, and Canyon de Chelly, which is free.
One way with no backtracking: 2,647 miles, and outside the Grand Canyon day barely a road driven twice.
New ground for this site. Oklahoma, the Texas Panhandle, New Mexico and the Navajo Nation are on no other route.
It gets warmer as it goes: eight cold nights, then Kingman, Barstow, Death Valley, Las Vegas and the beach.
Two nights in Williams and two in Death Valley, which is where the two days without a drive belong — and a train to the Grand Canyon rim from the first.
A night in Las Vegas on the way to the coast: the Welcome sign by daylight and the Bellagio fountains after dark, both free.
The only tolls are on day 1, and a free road runs beside them.
It finishes on a pier with a Ferris wheel, nine miles from the airport.
cons: 2,647 miles in fifteen days is 176 a day, against 110 on the Southwest Loop, with only two days off the road.
Eight nights in a row below freezing before Kingman, the coldest about −7°C at Holbrook and Monument Valley.
No Santa Fe: the Plaza, the Palace of the Governors and Loretto Chapel went with the cold, and Meow Wolf is now a car-only stop on the first morning.
Monument Valley gets an evening and a morning, not a day, and Albuquerque only an evening. That was the price of Tulsa and Petrified Forest.
Seven days are over 220 miles, the first of them straight off a flight, and day 5 adds three hours in Petrified Forest to 253 miles of driving.
Day 14 is 290 miles into Los Angeles on a Friday, on the second-last day.
The first three days are Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle in January: flat, brown and windy. It is a road trip before it is a scenery trip.
The western end overlaps the Las Vegas routes: Death Valley, the Grand Canyon, Monument Valley, Seligman, Oatman, Amboy and Las Vegas itself are each on at least one of them.
Both vehicles have to be hired one way, and only one of the big motorhome companies would do it from Dallas.

notConsidered.reason: It would not take a motorhome one way from Dallas to Los Angeles for these dates. El Monte would, from its depot in McKinney on day 1's road.
Owners on RVshare and Outdoorsy can allow a one-way trip, but they charge about $2 a mile to fetch it back from Los Angeles — more than the hire itself on a route this long.

notConsidered.place: The Oklahoma Route 66 Museum in Clinton
notConsidered.reason: Closed on Sundays and Mondays from November to January, and for the first week of January — day 3 is a Monday. The National Route 66 Museum at Elk City, 25 miles further on, is open Monday to Saturday all winter.

notConsidered.place: A rest day in Monument Valley
notConsidered.reason: It would have cost Petrified Forest and the Wigwam Motel, and those won. With a day there you would have sunrise and sunset, a guided tour into Mystery Valley and the Wildcat Trail. As planned it is sunset, sleep and the Valley Drive.

The first draft slept here, at 7,200 feet, where a January night averages about −8°C — which matters with a motorhome's plumbing live. Albuquerque is 1,900 feet lower and averages −3°C. It cost the Plaza, the Palace of the Governors and Loretto Chapel's staircase, and Meow Wolf, which is in Grapevine on day 1 instead, for the car.

At −10°C, the coldest average night anywhere on the first draft. Albuquerque to Holbrook is only 253 miles with Petrified Forest included, so it costs ten minutes in El Rancho's lobby rather than a night in it.

notConsidered.place: Two nights on the Grand Canyon rim
notConsidered.reason: Trailer Village and the rim lodges average −7°C in January, and both nights fell on Martin Luther King weekend at holiday prices. Williams is an hour south and barely a degree warmer, but it has a year-round RV park with full hookups beside the station and the train to the rim, so the motorhome sits plugged in all day. It costs sunrise at Mather Point.

notConsidered.place: Cameron as the Grand Canyon base
notConsidered.reason: The Cameron Trading Post RV Park is 2,600 feet lower than Williams, has full hookups, and is 57 miles from the Village — a fair base for day trips. Williams won for the train, and for a run to Kingman 40 miles shorter.
The first 650 miles of Route 66, through Illinois, Missouri and thirteen miles of Kansas, would need four or five more days. This trip starts where the flights land.

This plan sleeps there on night 13, then drives on to Los Angeles. Flying home from Las Vegas would save day 14 — but Route 66 would stop at Barstow, the finish on Santa Monica Pier would go, and four routes on this site already end there.

Flagstaff is on Route 66, but the line from Monument Valley to the Grand Canyon to Williams passes west of it, and Sedona is another 30 miles south with trails that are icy in January. It needs a day that does not exist.
85 extra miles between Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon, and the Southwest Loop already has them.

notConsidered.place: The Hopi mesas road from Holbrook
notConsidered.reason: The obvious-looking shortcut to Monument Valley, and the one a phone may pick, runs on unpaved BIA and Navajo roads. In January mud that is a bad idea in a car and a worse one in a motorhome. Ganado and Chinle are paved and pass Canyon de Chelly.

notConsidered.place: The Wigwam Motel in Rialto on night 14
notConsidered.reason: The other surviving Wigwam Motel on Route 66, in the San Bernardino valley. Sleeping there would cut day 14 to about five hours and put the last of the road on the final morning — but it only works with a flight home after about 4pm.
35 miles from the finish, but a day there for six is well over $1,000 in tickets alone, and there is no day to give it.
Both are 300 miles south of the route across empty New Mexico.
The Low Desert Loop has them, and they are 100 miles south of the Mojave stretch of 66.

moneySavers.item: Collect the car in town, not at the airport
moneySavers.detail: Airport counters add a concession recovery fee of around 11 per cent plus a daily facility charge. If the quote is from DFW or Love Field, price the same van from a neighbourhood branch nearby — a short taxi ride with the luggage — and dropping at LAX does not usually add the fees back.

The Dallas tollways and the Indian Nation Turnpike are cashless, and the hire company adds a daily fee to every toll it passes on. US-75 is free and about half an hour slower. After day 1 there is nothing to pay anywhere on the route.

moneySavers.item: Drive the motorhome up, not the train
moneySavers.detail: Coach seats for six are about $445. Driving the 60 miles each way costs about $45 in fuel and $36 in extra miles, and there is RV parking near the visitor centre — but it puts a 30-footer on an icy rim road and leaves it unplugged all day on the coldest stretch of the trip, which is why the train is in the plan.

moneySavers.item: Stovepipe Wells, not The Ranch at Furnace Creek
moneySavers.detail: Stovepipe Wells is inside the park, beside the dunes day 12 arrives at, and roughly half the price of The Ranch in peak season, which January is. Badwater is 25 miles further away each morning.

moneySavers.item: Drive the Monument Valley loop yourself
moneySavers.detail: In the car the 17-mile Valley Drive is included in the tribal entry. The guided tour is only needed for the closed parts — Mystery Valley and the arches — or if you would rather not take a hire car onto dirt.

moneySavers.item: Buy the park pass at Petrified Forest
moneySavers.detail: Three gates at $25, $35 and $30 against $80 for the pass. It barely pays on this route, but it also covers Wupatki, Walnut Canyon and anything else federal you add.

moneySavers.item: Ride the Ferris wheel, skip the wristband
moneySavers.detail: Pacific Park's unlimited-ride wristbands are priced for a day. For an hour on the pier at dusk, single tickets for the Ferris wheel and the roller coaster are a fraction of it.

moneySavers.item: Fill up in Arizona and Nevada
moneySavers.amount: ~$65 in the van, ~$190 in the motorhome
moneySavers.detail: California fuel runs more than a dollar a gallon over Arizona's and well over Nevada's. Leave Kingman on a full tank on day 10, time the next fill for Barstow rather than the Death Valley pumps, and fill up in Las Vegas before the drive into Los Angeles.

moneySavers.item: In the motorhome, pay for the extra miles, not unlimited
moneySavers.detail: El Monte's unlimited mileage is $1,135 for a hire this long. The plan needs about 1,200 miles over the 1,700 included, which at $30 for each 100 comes to about $390.

moneySavers.item: The Gold Package, not Peace of Mind on its own
moneySavers.detail: El Monte's Peace of Mind add-on is $15 a night, $210 for this trip. The Gold Package is $119 for the whole hire and includes Peace of Mind, the awning and additional drivers, which are otherwise $6 a night each. With VIP Plus you may not need it at all; if you do, buy it that way.

El Monte sells unlimited toll coverage at $5.95 to $19.95 a night. The motorhome never meets a toll: US-75 from McKinney to Tulsa, old 66 beside the Turner Turnpike, and nothing at all west of Oklahoma City.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: A hired seven-seater, fourteen rooms, and every road open
options.summary: The build this route is designed around. A seven-seater collected in Dallas and dropped at LAX, and a room every night — which matters here, because the first eight nights are below freezing. It is also the only way to drive everything on the route: the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive, Dante's View, Sitgreaves Pass and the Arroyo Seco are all barred to a 30-foot motorhome or no place for one. It costs more, and almost all of the gap is lodging and food.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Toyota Sienna · Chevrolet Suburban · one way, Dallas to Los Angeles
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count. A minivan is better for six people for fifteen days; a Suburban is better for their luggage. Nothing on the route needs four-wheel drive, but the first week crosses country that ices overnight — ask for tyres with tread on them. Read the agreement for two things: unpaved roads, because the Monument Valley loop is graded dirt, and Sitgreaves Pass.

lines.basis: Quoted: six seats, into Dallas on 9 January and home from LAX on the 23rd.
Quoted: $2,100 for a seven-seater one way, collected in Dallas on 9 January and dropped at LAX on the 23rd.

About 3,000 miles with the park roads and the drive up to the Grand Canyon from Williams, at around 21 mpg in a seven-seat minivan — a Suburban would add roughly $120. Around $3.00 a gallon in Texas and Oklahoma, $3.20 to $3.40 in New Mexico and Arizona, a little more in Nevada and $4.80 in California, on the EIA's forecast of $3.35 nationally for 2027.

Two rooms, or a family suite, every night. The dear nights are Death Valley in its peak season, Santa Monica on a Friday and, in the location column, the Strip. Williams on Martin Luther King weekend costs well under what the rim would.
Six people for fifteen days: hotel breakfasts, a diner lunch on the road, dinner out.
Hotel parking in Santa Monica, an evening's parking on the Strip, and a downtown night in Tulsa or Oklahoma City in the location column. Free almost everywhere else.
Covers Petrified Forest, the Grand Canyon and Death Valley — $90 at the gates.
Monument Valley at $8 to $10 a head, plus the Little Colorado River Gorge at $8 a head in the location column. The park pass is not valid at either.
Two and a half hours at about $79 an adult and $59 a child. In the value column you drive the loop yourself.
General admission from $35 an adult and $19 a child, or anytime entry from $44 and $24 in the location column. Day 1 only, and only if the flight lands early enough.
Elk City at $5 an adult and $4 a child, and Chandler's Interpretive Center.
The Ferris wheel for six in the value column, unlimited-ride wristbands in the other.
Spray paint at Cadillac Ranch, snacks at Pops, and Grand Canyon Caverns in the location column.

costs.notes: Best value sleeps in chain motels on the edge of each town, in Williams for the Grand Canyon, at Stovepipe Wells for Death Valley and off the Strip in Las Vegas, and drives the Monument Valley loop itself. Best location sleeps in Old Town Albuquerque, at The View in Monument Valley, beside the station in Williams, at The Ranch in Death Valley, on the Strip and by the beach in Santa Monica, and takes the Navajo-guided tour. The Wigwam Motel is the same in both.

pros: Every road on the route is open to you: the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive, Dante's View, Sitgreaves Pass and the Arroyo Seco.
Meow Wolf on the first morning, if the flight lands early — the bags stay in the car.
A heated room on each of the eight freezing nights.
Parks anywhere — Old Town Albuquerque, the Wigwam's forecourt, the Strip, Santa Monica Pier.
Around $700 less fuel than the motorhome.
Collected and returned at the airports, whenever the counters are open.
cons: Lodging and food are the two biggest lines in the budget.
Three children belted in for 2,600 miles, with nowhere to move.

1.label: Leave on US-75:
1.text: From Love Field it is two miles to US-75 with no toll road in between. From DFW, take I-635 east to US-75 rather than the Bush Turnpike.

1.label: Open to you:
1.text: Meow Wolf, if the flight lands by about nine. The Real Unreal is in Grapevine Mills, five miles from DFW, and opens at 10 on Saturdays. Bags are not allowed inside and the lockers are small, so leave everything in the car. Two or three hours there puts you in Tulsa around seven rather than half past five.

7.label: Open to you:
7.text: Drive the 17-mile Valley Drive yourself when the gate opens at 8. It is graded dirt, and most hire agreements exclude unpaved roads — go slowly and stay on the loop, or book the guided tour instead.

8.label: Open to you:
8.text: Drive up rather than taking the train, and you have Hermit Road, seven miles out to Hermits Rest. Private cars are allowed only from December to February and only under 22 feet, which a minivan or a Suburban is. Hopi Point for sunset, then an hour back to Williams in the dark — watch for elk on AZ-64.

10.label: Open to you:
10.text: Sitgreaves Pass, the real Route 66 over the Black Mountains into Oatman: eight miles of hairpins with no shoulders. Legal for anything under 40 feet — check the hire agreement, which may say otherwise.

12.label: Open to you:
12.text: Artist's Drive and the last climb to Dante's View, both closed to vehicles over 25 feet.

14.label: Open to you:
14.text: The Arroyo Seco Parkway, America's first freeway, which carries Route 66 from Pasadena into downtown. It was built for 45 mph, and the on-ramps start from a stop sign.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheaper, colder, and shut out of six places
options.summary: A Class C from El Monte's depot in McKinney — thirty miles up US-75, on day 1's road — returned to their yard in Santa Fe Springs, twenty miles from LAX. Cruise America would not take one this far one way; El Monte will. It is still the cheaper build, and the long Oklahoma and Texas days go easier when the children can get up and move about. The overnight stops are picked with it in mind: Albuquerque rather than Santa Fe, no night in Gallup, and two nights plugged in beside the station in Williams, taking the train to the rim rather than driving a 30-footer up an icy road. But this is still the hardest route on the site for a motorhome: eight freezing nights in a row with live plumbing, a 1pm handover that puts the end of day 1 in the dark and rules out Meow Wolf, about 1,200 miles over the quote's allowance, and six places on the route where it is barred or unwise.

vehicle.detail: El Monte Class C Family Sleeper · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30–32 ft long · about 8 mpg · one way, McKinney TX to Santa Fe Springs CA
vehicle.notes: Ask for the Family Sleeper by name: it has seven seatbelts, where El Monte's Class C Large has exactly six and is rated for four adults and two children. At 30 to 32 feet it is too long for Hermit Road's 22-foot limit and for Death Valley's 25-foot roads, as any Class C this size is. Confirm that the water system is live and the unit is not winterized: this route has eight freezing nights before it warms up.

lines.basis: Quoted: six seats, into Dallas on 9 January and home from LAX on the 23rd.
Quoted by El Monte: McKinney to Santa Fe Springs, 9 to 23 January, with 1,700 miles included.

About 2,900 miles in the motorhome — the day routes, the Canyon de Chelly rim, Death Valley's side roads and ten miles a day around campgrounds and supermarkets — at $30 for each 100 over. The high column allows another 300.

lines.item: Peace of Mind, as the Gold Package
lines.basis: Only if El Monte says the VIP Plus cover does not pay for a windscreen. Then take the Gold Package, $119 for the hire with Peace of Mind, the awning and extra drivers, rather than Peace of Mind alone at $15 a night. Breakdowns and 24/7 roadside support are included either way.
About 2,900 miles at 8 to 9 mpg, on the same regional prices as the car — Texas and Oklahoma cheapest, California dearest.
Full hookups where they are open — an Albuquerque park off I-40, Goulding's, the Grand Canyon Railway RV Park, Stovepipe Wells and the Oasis in Las Vegas — and Dockweiler for the last night.
Cooking in the motorhome, with a few meals out on the Route 66 days.
Bought on the way out of Dallas rather than paying per-person kit fees.
Covers Petrified Forest, the Grand Canyon and Death Valley — $90 at the gates.
$8 to $10 a head; the park pass is not valid.
The only way onto the valley floor in a motorhome. The low column settles for the view from the rim and the Wildcat Trail.

Six seats to the South Rim and back from Williams: Coach at about $90 an adult and $58 a child in 2026, or First Class at about $140 and $110 in the high column. The adult fares include a $15 park fee.
Elk City at $5 an adult and $4 a child, and Chandler's Interpretive Center.
The Ferris wheel for six, or unlimited-ride wristbands.
Propane, dump fees, laundry, showers, taxis to the Strip from the Las Vegas RV park, and parking a 30-footer in Los Angeles.

costs.notes: The hire is El Monte's quote, one way with 1,700 miles. The low column adds only the miles the plan needs, the cheapest open campground at each stop, Coach seats on the train, and no guided tour or add-on. The high column allows 300 more miles, takes the Gold Package, the Monument Valley tour, First Class on the train and the Pacific Park wristbands.

pros: Cheapest by a margin.
The kitchen: breakfasts and lunches in, and the long days across Oklahoma and Texas go easier when three children can get up.
No check-ins at fourteen stops.
Two nights on full hookups beside the Williams station, and a short walk to the train — the motorhome stays plugged in while you are at the rim.
The last night is at Dockweiler, a county campground on the beach.
cons: Eight nights below freezing in a row, with live plumbing.
Barred from the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive and the top of Dante's View; no place for it on Sitgreaves Pass or the Arroyo Seco.
A 1pm handover in McKinney puts the end of day 1 in the dark, and leaves nowhere for the bags if you wanted Meow Wolf first.
Around $700 more fuel than the car.
About 1,200 miles over the 1,700 the hire includes, at $30 for each 100.

1.label: Late away:
1.text: El Monte's Dallas depot is in McKinney, 30 miles up US-75 and on the way — take a taxi from the airport. Pickup is after 1pm and the handover takes one to two hours, so you leave about 3 for the 238 miles to Tulsa, the last two of them in the dark. Book the Tulsa site for a late arrival.

1.label: No Meow Wolf:
1.text: Grapevine does not allow luggage inside and its lockers are small, and the motorhome is not yours until after 1pm in McKinney, forty miles the other way. With Santa Fe off the route, the motorhome build loses Meow Wolf altogether.

1.label: Freezing from the first night.
1.text: Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump, which stops working around 4°C. Disconnect the city-water hose at night and run off the fresh tank; the hose freezes long before the tanks do.

4.label: Open all winter:
4.text: Albuquerque's RV parks stay open — the KOA Journey and American RV Resort, both just off I-40, have full hookups. Fill the propane here; the next planned fill is Williams.

5.label: No hookups at the Wigwam:
5.text: Sleep at one of Holbrook's RV parks and walk over for the photographs — or book a wigwam for the night and leave the motorhome outside.

6.label: Hookups at Goulding’s:
6.text: Goulding's campground has full hookups; The View's is dry camping only, on one of the coldest nights of the trip. Call ahead to check which is open in January.

7.label: Not in the motorhome:
7.text: The Navajo Nation bars RVs from the Valley Drive. The rim at the visitor centre and the 3.2-mile Wildcat Trail are free; a Navajo-guided tour — about $79 an adult and $59 a child — is the only way onto the valley floor.

7.label: Sleep beside the station:
7.text: The Grand Canyon Railway RV Park in Williams is open all winter, with full hookups on 124 paved sites next to the depot. Two nights, and you walk to the train.

8.label: Take the train:
8.text: Leave the motorhome plugged in at the depot and ride up. It stays on shore power with the furnace running all day, and nobody drives a 30-footer on an icy rim road. The return leaves the rim before sunset.

8.label: Not in the motorhome:
8.text: Hermit Road is private cars only in winter, and only under 22 feet, and no shuttle runs it until March. You have Mather and Yavapai Points, the Village rim and the Rim Trail.

10.label: Not over Sitgreaves Pass.
10.text: The map takes I-40 from Kingman to Needles and rejoins the car at Amboy. If the burros matter, come at Oatman from the flat side — up from Topock and out on Boundary Cone Road — for about 48 more miles and two more hours.

11.label: Low gear:
11.text: Towne Pass drops almost 5,000 feet into Stovepipe Wells. Use the gears, not the brakes.

12.label: Not in the motorhome:
12.text: Artist's Drive and the last climb to Dante's View are closed to vehicles over 25 feet. Badwater, Devil's Golf Course and Golden Canyon are open to you.

13.label: Sleep at the Oasis:
13.text: Oasis Las Vegas RV Resort, a mile and a half from the Welcome sign, has full hookups on concrete pads. Take a taxi to the Bellagio rather than hunting for somewhere on the Strip to leave 30 feet of motorhome; the lot at the sign has two bus bays.

14.label: Not on the Arroyo Seco.
14.text: Narrow 1940 lanes, tight curves and stop-sign on-ramps are no place for a 30-footer. The map takes I-10 instead.

14.label: Sleep at Dockweiler.
14.text: Santa Monica does not let oversized vehicles park on its streets overnight without a permit. Dockweiler RV Park, the county's beach campground nine miles south under the LAX flight path, takes bookings no more than 90 days ahead — book it the day that window opens.

15.label: Back in the morning:
15.text: Return it to El Monte in Santa Fe Springs, 23 miles from Dockweiler, in their morning window (9 to 10:30 at McKinney), then take a taxi the 23 miles to LAX. Book a flight after about 1pm.

days.headline: Fly in, then US-75 all the way north
days.notes: Land, collect the vehicle and point it north. US-75 runs from Dallas to Tulsa without a toll — the faster turnpike route bills you through the hire company — and crosses the Red River into Oklahoma about an hour out. It is the longest first day of any route on this site that starts with a flight, and you arrive after dark, which in Tulsa in January is about half past five. Keep the evening small: the Meadow Gold sign lit up on 11th Street, which is Route 66, and dinner. In the car, an early landing at DFW buys a morning at Meow Wolf in Grapevine first. Tulsa: highs around 9°C, lows around −2°C.

days.headline: The best 150 miles of old 66 in Oklahoma
days.notes: Slow on purpose. East first to the Blue Whale at Catoosa, then back through Tulsa and west on the two-lane that runs beside the Turner Turnpike rather than on it — Sapulpa, Kellyville, Bristow, Depew — for lunch at the Rock Café in Stroud. Then the Route 66 Interpretive Center in Chandler's 1937 armory, the Round Barn at Arcadia, and the 66-foot soda bottle at Pops. It is a Sunday, which is the catch: Chandler opens only from 1 to 5, and that is exactly when you pass. Oklahoma City: highs around 10°C, lows around −2°C.

days.headline: Into the Panhandle, and Cadillacs at sunset
days.notes: I-40 replaced Route 66 out here and mostly runs on top of it, so this is interstate with stops. Skip Clinton's museum — it is shut on Mondays in winter and for the first week of January — and use the National Route 66 Museum at Elk City, 25 miles on, which is open. Then the U-Drop Inn at Shamrock, the 1936 art deco Conoco station that became Ramone's in Cars, and Groom's water tower, tilted on purpose in 1980 to pull drivers off the interstate. Reach Cadillac Ranch for the last hour of light — sunset is about 5:55 — and bring a can of spray paint, because everyone does. Amarillo: highs around 10°C, lows around −5°C.

days.headline: New Mexico, and Route 66 down Central Avenue
days.notes: You gain an hour at the New Mexico line. Tucumcari's motel strip first — the Blue Swallow's sign is worth the stop even by day — then the Blue Hole at Santa Rosa, a spring 80 feet deep and the colour of a swimming pool, where divers train all winter. From Santa Rosa, I-40 follows the 1937 alignment straight west into Albuquerque by mid-afternoon. Central Avenue is Route 66 through the middle of the city, and the KiMo Theatre on it is Pueblo Deco from 1927. Old Town, a mile and a half further west, keeps its plaza and San Felipe de Neri, a church that has stood on it since 1793. Albuquerque sits at 5,300 feet: highs around 9°C, lows around −3°C.

days.headline: Over the Divide to the only national park on Route 66
days.notes: The long day of the first week, so leave by half past eight. I-40 climbs west over the Continental Divide at about 7,250 feet and past Gallup, where El Rancho — built in 1937 for the film crews making Westerns — is worth ten minutes in the lobby if you are ahead of time. Petrified Forest is open 8 to 5 in winter, and opens late when the road is icy. Come in from I-40 at the north end, 207 miles from Albuquerque: the Painted Desert overlooks, the Painted Desert Inn, and the pullout where a line of telephone poles and a rusted 1932 Studebaker mark where Route 66 crossed the park. South from there past the Newspaper Rock petroglyphs, the Blue Mesa loop — a mile's walk down among blue and purple badlands — and Agate Bridge, and out past the Giant Logs behind the Rainbow Forest Museum. 28 miles of park road and about three hours; leave Albuquerque on time and you reach the north gate around half past twelve, with an hour in hand before the gates close at five. Then Holbrook and the Wigwam Motel, fifteen concrete teepees with old cars parked outside. Holbrook: highs around 11°C, lows around −7°C.

days.headline: Across the Navajo Nation to the Mittens
days.notes: North on US-191 through Ganado and Chinle, which is paved all the way — not the shortcut across the Hopi mesas that a phone may suggest, which runs on Navajo and BIA dirt roads that are mud in January. Hubbell Trading Post at Ganado has traded with Navajo families since 1878 and is still a working store; it is free. At Chinle, Canyon de Chelly's South Rim Drive runs 18 miles out to Spider Rock, an 800-foot sandstone spire, past the White House Overlook above a cliff dwelling. It is free, but it adds about 36 miles and two hours, so this is a long day. Then 110 miles to Monument Valley for sunset over the Mittens at about 5:25. The Valley Drive's last entry in winter is 2:30, so the loop is tomorrow. Monument Valley: highs around 6°C, lows around −7°C.

days.headline: The Valley Drive at eight, the canyon rim by three
days.notes: Be at the gate when it opens at 8. The 17-mile Valley Drive is graded dirt — slow and bumpy, fine when dry — and takes about two and a half hours with John Ford's Point and the Three Sisters. Out by 11, then back through Kayenta, where the Burger King has long kept a small exhibit on the Navajo Code Talkers (worth ten minutes if it is still up), Tuba City and Cameron, whose 1916 trading post does a proper lunch. The Little Colorado River Gorge overlook on AZ-64 is a Navajo tribal park at $8 a head, with a sheer drop of about a thousand feet. You enter the Grand Canyon at Desert View, the best first look there is, and follow the rim west for 25 miles past Lipan, Moran and Grandview Points to the Village, then leave by the south gate for the hour down AZ-64 to Williams. Stay at the rim for sunset at about 5:25 and you reach Williams around seven; tomorrow is a whole day up there, so there is no need. It is the Friday of Martin Luther King weekend. Williams: highs around 7°C, lows around −6°C.

days.headline: A whole day on the South Rim, by train or by road
days.notes: Two ways up. The Grand Canyon Railway leaves from the depot in the middle of Williams every morning: about two and a quarter hours each way through ponderosa pine, a little under four hours at the rim, and a return that leaves before sunset. Or drive the 60 miles up AZ-64, which is the only way to stay for sunset. Either way the Village is where the rim is best on foot: Mather Point and the heated Yavapai Geology Museum, the paved Rim Trail between them, and the top of the Bright Angel Trail, which drops straight off the edge — go down to the first switchbacks and turn round, and wear traction if it is icy. From December to February, and only then, Hermit Road is open to private cars under 22 feet: seven miles out to Hermits Rest, with Hopi Point for sunset at about 5:30. It is the Saturday of Martin Luther King weekend, so book the train ahead. Williams: highs around 7°C, lows around −6°C.

days.headline: Back on 66 for the longest stretch left
days.notes: The short day of the second week. Williams first, in daylight: the last town on Route 66 to be bypassed by the interstate — in October 1984 — and still built around it. Then Seligman, where Angel Delgadillo's barbershop started the campaign that saved the road; his family's Snow Cap drive-in is closed for the winter, but the gift shops are not. From Seligman to Kingman, 66 swings north away from I-40 on the longest unbroken stretch of the old road left anywhere: Peach Springs, Grand Canyon Caverns (a lift 21 storeys down into a dry cave, if you want it), and the Hackberry General Store with its forecourt of old cars and pumps. If snow has cost you time earlier in the week, this is the day that gives it back. Kingman: highs around 13°C, lows around −1°C.

days.headline: Burros, Roy's, and the empty Mojave
days.notes: Route 66 climbs out of Kingman over Sitgreaves Pass — eight miles of hairpins with no shoulders — and drops into Oatman, a gold-mining town kept alive by the wild burros that wander its main street. They come to the car window; the shops sell bags of burro food and ask you to use that. You gain an hour crossing the Colorado River into California at Needles. Then I-40 to Kelbaker Road and the old road west to Roy's at Amboy, the 1938 motel and café with the sign everyone photographs; the café was being restored for the road's centennial, so check before counting on lunch there. Late lunch instead at the Bagdad Café in Newberry Springs, from the 1987 film. Barstow: highs around 16°C, lows around 2°C.

days.headline: Into Death Valley the back way
days.notes: West out of Barstow and north through Trona and the Panamint Valley, rather than east through Baker. It is 17 miles longer, and it means no road on this trip is driven twice, because day 14 comes through Baker from Las Vegas. It comes into the park over Towne Pass at 4,956 feet and drops almost 5,000 feet to Stovepipe Wells. Walk out onto the Mesquite Flat Dunes on the way through, then on to Furnace Creek, 190 feet below sea level, and Zabriskie Point for sunset at about five. Death Valley: highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

days.headline: Below sea level, and warm
days.notes: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America, 282 feet below sea level, and about 18°C in January. Walk out onto the salt there first, then Devil's Golf Course, Artist's Drive — a one-way loop through hills stained green and pink — and the easy walk up Golden Canyon. End the day at Dante's View, 5,475 feet straight above Badwater. The park is still repairing flood damage, so check its conditions page the week before. Highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

days.headline: Out of the valley at sunrise, and a night in Las Vegas
days.notes: Zabriskie Point at sunrise, a little before seven, on the way out — the badlands go gold first. Then east past Death Valley Junction, where Marta Becket painted an audience on the walls of the Amargosa Opera House and danced for it for more than forty years, over the Nevada line to Pahrump, and into Las Vegas by lunchtime. The Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign has a small free lot in the median at the south end of the Strip. After dark the Fountains of Bellagio go off every fifteen minutes from 8 until midnight, and every half hour from 3 before that on a weekday. They are free, and so is the conservatory beside them, though it shuts while it changes displays in January — check before you count on it. Las Vegas: highs around 14°C, lows around 4°C.

days.headline: The last of Route 66, and the Pacific
days.notes: With day 4, the longest drive of the trip, so leave by eight and fill up before you leave Nevada. South on I-15 past Baker and its 134-foot thermometer, through Barstow and down Cajon Pass into the Los Angeles basin. Route 66's own line across the valley is Foothill Boulevard, thirty miles of traffic lights past the Wigwam Motel in Rialto; this route takes the parallel I-210 and rejoins 66 on Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena. From there the Arroyo Seco Parkway — America's first freeway, opened in 1940 and still with stop-sign on-ramps — carries it into downtown, and I-10 runs to the ocean. Aim to be past Pasadena before two, when the Friday traffic builds. The pier at dusk, with the Ferris wheel lit. Santa Monica: highs around 18°C, lows around 9°C.

days.headline: The End of the Trail sign, then home
days.notes: Walk out to the End of the Trail sign first thing, before the pier fills up — the photograph every Route 66 trip ends with. The legal end of the road is a mile inland, at Lincoln and Olympic, and nobody photographs that. Then nine miles to LAX. The car goes back at the airport; the motorhome goes back to Carson, which changes the morning.
